title: Letta (MemGPT)
by: Letta, the team behind MemGPT. Read from the letta README, the letta-code README, and the archived server's memory tools (letta/functions/function_sets/base.py) and block schema (letta/schemas/block.py) on the archive branch. docs.letta.com and arxiv.org were blocked; the MemGPT and sleep-time papers were not read.
summary: An agent harness whose memory lives in the agent's own context as labelled blocks it edits with tools. Blocks have a label, a value, a character limit, a description and a read-only flag. Older text goes to archival memory, reached by insert and search tools. A second, sleep-time agent (now called dreaming) rewrites the blocks between conversations, and Letta Code tracks all of this context in git.
ideas: Memory blocks: label, value, limit, description, read_only; they sit in the context window, so the agent always sees them.
Edit tools with exact names: core_memory_append and core_memory_replace (first set), later memory_replace, memory_insert, memory_apply_patch and memory_rethink, plus memory_finish_edits.
memory_replace needs an exact match of the old string, like a code edit; memory_rethink rewrites a whole block and is meant for reorganising, not small fixes.
Archival memory is outside the context: archival_memory_insert and archival_memory_search; conversation_search reads past messages.
Sleep-time agents (dreaming) do the consolidation in the background, so the main agent answers fast.
Letta Code's MemFS keeps all context, memory blocks included, in git, and can sync it to a GitHub repo.

took.idea: Fixed edit tools with exact-match replace, refused when the old text is not found
Read-only docs the agent may read but not write
Consolidation as a separate background step, not part of every write
Agent memory kept as files in git
